repairs.after: {"q": "How many of the not-yet-migrated services call the deprecated watchAndReload API that Helix does not implement, and when is the compatibility shim expected?", "answer": "96 remaining services still call watchAndReload; the compatibility shim has an ETA of Oct 9 2026", "accept": ["96; Oct 9", "96 services affected, shim expected Oct 9 2026 after code review"]}
repairs.rationale: This is the status_update instance of the defect the verify pass found in design_doc-02-q1. The first pass rewrote accept[0] from '96; October 9' to '96; Oct 9 2026'. That killed the single-token key ['october'], but '96; Oct 9 2026' normalises to '96 oct 9 2026' in which every token except '2026' is three characters or shorter, so the lexical word list collapsed to ['2026'] - one token, matched by substring. I ran it both ways: 'The compatibility shim is expected in 2026.' and 'The shim ETA is Oct 9 2026.' are rejected by the old key and scored CORRECT by the new one. The second is worse than the first, because it answers half the question - it never gives the 96 - and this brief dates everything in 2026 (Apr 6 2026, Dec 12 2026, Feb 28 2027), so a bare year is the cheapest token in the document. Probing that led me to check the item's other three keys, and all three are sieves on the same branch: accept[1] '96, with the shim landing Oct 9' reduces to ['with','shim','landing'] and scores 'The shim is landing with the release.'; accept[2] '96 remaining services; ETA Oct 9 2026' reduces to ['remaining','services','2026'] and scores 'The remaining services will be migrated in 2026.'; accept[3] '96 - shim in code review, ETA Oct 9' reduces to ['shim','code','review'] and scores 'The compatibility shim is in code review.'. The canonical is no better: ['services','shim','2026'] scores 'The shim for those services is expected in 2026.'. Four number-free replies scoring on a question that asks for a count and a date. Repairing accept[0] alone would have left a precise key beside three loose ones. Rebuilt so every key is either numeric-only or long. The canonical now carries eight content words and needs seven, which no short reply reaches. accept[0] is '96; Oct 9' - every token three characters or shorter, so its lexical word list is empty and the lexical branch is disabled outright; it grades purely on the number set {96, 9}, which is the floor the correct answer permits (a reply writing 'Oct 9', '9 October' or '10/9' all satisfy it, and one writing only 96 or only the date does not). accept[1] is an eight-word rendering needing seven. I did not keep a spelled-out variant: the brief writes 96 in digits and no writer spells a two-digit count out, and any spelled key that still wrote a digit would reintroduce a weak number set. Verified against a replica of tools/comprehension.py. Fail: the four lexical-sieve replies above, the stem echo, 'The write-up talks about services.', a count-only reply, a date-only reply, an October-only reply, a wrong-count reply, and NOT STATED - eleven in total. Pass: 'Oct 9' and '9 October' and '10/9' renderings, with and without the year, reordered, terse, and in prose - seven in total.

repairs.after: {"q": "As of Sep 18 2026, how many services had been cut over to Helix, out of how many total in scope, and what percentage is that?", "answer": "744 of 1,240, 60%", "accept": ["744 of 1240 services migrated, 60% of the fleet", "744/1,240 = 60%", "60% - 744 of 1,240", "60% (744/1240)"]}
repairs.rationale: Found by running the same probe across the rest of the brief; pre-existing rather than repair-induced, but it is the identical collapse and it sits in the item next door. accept[0] '744 of 1240, 60%' normalises to tokens '744', 'of', '1240', '60%', of which only '1240' survives the len>3 filter, so the lexical key is the single token ['1240'] and the reply '1240 services are in scope.' - the denominator alone, no migrated count, no percentage - scores CORRECT. Only accept[0] changes; the canonical and the other three accepts are left exactly as the first pass verified them. The no-comma number set {744, 1240, 60} that accept[0] existed to carry is preserved in the replacement and is also already carried by accept[3] '60% (744/1240)', so nothing is lost; the replacement adds three content words so the lexical list needs all four of ['1240','services','migrated','fleet'] rather than one. Verified: 'nine lazy replies now fail (denominator alone in both comma conventions, numerator alone in two phrasings, percentage alone, the stem echo, the topic sentence, and NOT STATED) and six correct renderings still pass (comma, no-comma, slash, reordered, no-comma slash, and full prose).
